stories.title: JLL Lists Chelsea’s Rubin Museum for Sale
stories.excerpt: JLL has been retained by the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art to market its New York City flagship location for sale. Located at 140–154 W. 17th St. in Chelsea, the property represents a rare opportunity to reposition a historically and architecturally significant asset at the nexus of Chelsea, the Flatiron District and Greenwich Village, according to JLL. The 80,000-square-foot mixed-use site features a six-story former museum property totaling roughly 52,000 square feet, complemented by an adjacent and contiguous residential component with 46 apartments. “This is a truly one-of-a-kind asset in New York City,” said David Carlos, vice chairman and head of JLL’s Nonprofit, Education & Government Practice. “Its rich history, institutional-quality infrastructure and architectural character make it exceptionally well-suited for a variety of uses. Opportunities like this, where a property can seamlessly adapt to cultural, educational, commercial or mixed-use applications, are extraordinarily rare in today’s market.” The post JLL Lists Chelsea’s Rubin Museum for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL marketing 80,000 SF mixed-use at 140–154 W. 17th St., Chelsea, NYC—52K SF museum + 46 apartments
Property positioned for cultural, educational, commercial, or residential repositioning in high-demand Chelsea/Flatiron nexus
Rare institutional-quality asset with significant adaptive-use optionality in constrained Manhattan market
stories.summary: JLL has been retained to market the Rubin Museum's flagship property in Chelsea—an 80,000-square-foot mixed-use asset comprising a six-story former museum (52,000 SF) and 46 residential units. The site is located at the intersection of Chelsea, Flatiron, and Greenwich Village. The property is described as rare and architecturally significant, with institutional-quality infrastructure suited to multiple uses including cultural, educational, commercial, or residential applications.
stories.impact: For multifamily developers, this signals potential acquisition of a 46-unit existing residential component or repositioning of the entire site for rental housing in one of Manhattan's most expensive and supply-constrained neighborhoods. The museum's exit and the 52,000 SF commercial footprint present an opportunity for ground-up or conversion-based development that could yield significantly higher-density residential; however, historic designation and neighborhood character protections will likely cap upside and extend entitlement timelines.

stories.title: Gantry Arranges Life Company Loan on Temecula Offices
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $9-million life company loan to retire a CMBS loan on Vail Ranch Town Square, a low-rise suburban office building located at 32605 Temecula Pkwy. in Temecula. Principal Tony Kaufmann and associates Toby Judge and Jake Davis with the firm’s San Francisco production office represented the borrower, a private real estate investor in Southern California. The fixed rate, three-year loan featured a rate lock at application that protected the borrower in a rising rate environment. Gantry will service the loan for the lender. The three-story, 55,000-square-foot, Mediterranean-style building is 100%-leased to a range of medical, dental, behavioral health and professional service tenants. The location offers abundant surface parking and ready access to nearby retail, dining, and residential neighborhoods. Kaufmann said, “The case for office continues to improve and Gantry’s roster of life company lenders are showing an increasing willingness to fund new loans on performing assets.” The post Gantry Arranges Life Company Loan on Temecula Offices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry arranges $9M life company loan on 55K SF office, Temecula, CA—100% leased, three-year fixed term
Life company lenders showing increased willingness to fund performing office assets in rising-rate environment
Refinance from CMBS to life company debt signals market stabilization and alternative capital availability
stories.summary: Gantry closed a $9 million life company loan to retire a CMBS loan on Vail Ranch Town Square, a 55,000-square-foot, fully leased medical and professional services office building in Temecula, California. The three-year fixed-rate loan featured a rate lock at application. The property is 100% occupied by medical, dental, behavioral health, and professional service tenants and includes abundant surface parking.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, the increased appetite from life company lenders for performing commercial assets—and willingness to extend fixed-rate terms—suggests modest improvement in capital availability across CRE. This could ease refinancing pressure on multifamily loans but does not signal new demand tailwinds or supply constraints in Temecula market.

stories.title: Brooklyn Navy Yard Brings New Rotation of Small Businesses to Yard Opportunity Shop
stories.excerpt: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation (BNYDC) announced the third rotation of small businesses at its Yard Opportunity Shop (YOS) storefront. Now entering its third season, the YOS x Made in NYC Bodega will bring Doosra, Gracie Baked, Live Loud Foods and Oso Cacao together under one roof. Hosted in Building 92 of the Brooklyn Navy Yard, the three-month YOS rotations give small, minority-and-women-owned businesses (MWBEs) the opportunity to promote their products, test new concepts and directly engage with the Brooklyn community. YOS is part of BNYDC’s growing pipeline of initiatives supporting local MWBE retail entrepreneurs. “New York’s food scene is one of the most dynamic in the world, driven by entrepreneurs who are constantly reimagining what a product, a menu or a business can be,” said Lindsay Greene, president and CEO of the BNYDC. “We want the Navy Yard to be a place where that kind of innovation has room to grow.” The post Brooklyn Navy Yard Brings New Rotation of Small Businesses to Yard Opportunity Shop appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corp. launches third rotation of small businesses at Yard Opportunity Shop, Building 92
YOS x Made in NYC Bodega supports MWBEs via three-month retail activation cycles—food/beverage focus
BNYDC initiative signals continued mixed-use activation and community-oriented programming at Navy Yard campus
stories.summary: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation announced the third rotation of small businesses at its Yard Opportunity Shop (YOS) in Building 92. The YOS x Made in NYC Bodega will host four minority- and women-owned food businesses (Doosra, Gracie Baked, Live Loud Foods, Oso Cacao) in a three-month pop-up cycle. YOS is part of BNYDC's broader pipeline to support local MWBE retail entrepreneurs.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. The retail and food-service activation at Navy Yard complements mixed-use residential development in the neighborhood and signals robust ground-floor programming and tenant mix—factors that support rental desirability. However, this is a programmatic announcement, not a supply or demand shock; it reinforces existing Navy Yard positioning as a vibrant mixed-use destination rather than signaling new residential demand or constraints.

stories.title: Value-Add Rentals Go for $13M in El Cajon
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 229 Shady Ln., a circa-1969, 59-unit multifamily property located in El Cajon. The asset sold for $13.25 million, or $224,576 per unit. “Value-add apartment communities in East County San Diego continue to attract investor interest because of strong renter demand, limited housing supply and opportunities to improve operations over time,” said Austin Huffman, senior director investments. “Villa Capri offered an attractive combination of spacious floor plans, upgraded property systems and meaningful rental upside, making it a compelling acquisition for an investor seeking long-term value.” Huffman and Christopher Zorbas, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s San Diego office, represented the seller, Mary Susan Curry 2020 Revocable Living Trust, and procured the buyer, TFT Capital I. The property is located near Interstate 8, the El Cajon Transit Center and major employment centers throughout San Diego County. The buyer plans to renovate the property to enhance its long-term value. The post Value-Add Rentals Go for $13M in El Cajon appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sells 59-unit circa-1969 property, El Cajon, for $13.25M ($224.6K/unit); buyer is TFT Capital I
Value-add thesis: strong renter demand, limited housing supply, operational upside in East County San Diego
Property near I-8, transit center, major employment hubs; buyer plans renovations to enhance long-term value
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of Villa Capri, a 59-unit multifamily property built in 1969 at 229 Shady Lane in El Cajon, for $13.25 million ($224,576 per unit). The buyer, TFT Capital I, plans renovation and repositioning. The property is located near Interstate 8, the El Cajon Transit Center, and major employment centers throughout San Diego County. Marcus & Millichap cited strong renter demand and limited housing supply in East County as key investment drivers.
stories.impact: Validation of value-add thesis in East County San Diego market—strong absorption, limited new supply, and employer proximity support rent growth and investor returns. The sub-$225K/unit entry price on a renovatable asset signals continued investor confidence in San Diego's Inland Empire submarkets. Developers should monitor job growth and population migration into East County; lack of new supply and strong fundamentals may create window for new construction or land acquisition before rents and cap rates fully adjust.

stories.title: The Learning Experience Plans Expansion in NY Tri-State, Upstate NY
stories.excerpt: Childcare franchise The Learning Experience plans to add nine locations across the New York Tri-State area and five in Upstate New York over the next 18 months. The company currently operates 43 locations in the Tri-State region. Plans call for a new Learning Experience location in Fair Lawn, NJ during the fourth quarter of 2026. It will be followed by new sites in Monroe, CT (Q1 2027); Islip, NY (Q3 2027); Sparta, NJ (Q4 2027); Old Bridge, NJ (Q4 2027); Port Jefferson Station, NY (Q1 2028); East Meadow, NY (Q1 2028); Hauppauge, NY (Q1 2028); and Belleville, NJ (Q2 2028). In addition to the New York City market, The Learning Experience plans to open three new locations in the Syracuse area (Liverpool, Clay and Syracuse), one in Albany, and one near Buffalo in East Amherst. Those openings run from Q3 2027 through Q1 2028. Each location will consist of up to 10,000 square feet of indoor building space with up to a 5,000-square-foot playground. The post The Learning Experience Plans Expansion in NY Tri-State, Upstate NY appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Learning Experience plans 14 new childcare locations across NY Tri-State (9) and Upstate NY (5) over 18 months
Currently operates 43 tri-state locations; first new site opens Fair Lawn, NJ Q4 2026; pipeline through Q1 2028
Locations range 10K SF indoor + 5K SF outdoor playground; expansion targets high-income suburban/metro corridors
stories.summary: Childcare franchise The Learning Experience plans to add nine locations across the New York Tri-State region and five in Upstate New York over the next 18 months, growing from 43 current tri-state locations. The first location opens in Fair Lawn, NJ in Q4 2026, followed by sites in Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Syracuse, Albany, and Buffalo through Q1 2028. Each location will comprise up to 10,000 square feet of indoor space plus a 5,000-square-foot playground.
stories.impact: Signal of family-household demand and affluent residential growth across NY metro and Upstate. Childcare expansion into underserved suburban nodes (Islip, Hauppauge, East Meadow on Long Island; Monroe, CT; Syracuse, Albany, Buffalo) suggests demographic migration toward outer rings and secondary metros. For multifamily developers, this reinforces demand for family-friendly, suburban-adjacent communities with nearby employment and amenities in Northeast markets; landlords should track childcare availability as a renter retention lever, especially for 2+ bedroom units targeting young families.

stories.title: Distyl AI Doubles Its 135 Madison Offices to 30K SF After Less Than a Year
stories.excerpt: Software development company Distyl AI has room to grow. The artificial intelligence-powered developer of operating systems for large companies has leased the entire ninth floor at 135 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, according to building manager Koeppel Rosen, bringing the company’s total footprint to 30,076 square feet. Distyl AI arrived at the Rosen family’s 13-story building in December 2025, Commercial Observer reported at the time, initially taking 15,038 square feet across the entire 10th floor. Asking rent for the recent expansion was $55 per square foot, and both leases run through January 2028, according to Crain’s New York Business, which first reported the lease. Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel represented the Rosen family in the transaction, while Justin Pollner and Steven Rotter of Newmark negotiated on behalf of Distyl AI. Distyl AI’s arrival at 135 Madison in December represented the company’s first office in New York City and second location overall, after establishing its headquarters at 55 Hawthorne Street in San Francisco in 2022. “We were pleased to work with Distyl AI to reconfigure and expand its footprint across two contiguous floors at 135 Madison Avenue,” Koeppel said in a statement. “We celebrate the company’s rapidly growing operations, which required additional office space.” The office building on the corner of East 31st Street and Madison Avenue is also home to health care technology platform Courier Health, coworking firm WeWork, digital marketing firm Demand Growth Digital, e-commerce marketing company Mobikasa and event space provider Blender Workspace. A spokesperson for Distyl AI did not immediately respond to a requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Distyl AI (AI/software) leases entire 9th floor at 135 Madison, NoMad, doubling footprint to 30.1K SF in <1 year
Expansion lease at $55/SF through Jan. 2028; company relocated from San Francisco HQ to NYC in Dec. 2025
High-growth tech tenant signals continued appeal of Manhattan's tech ecosystem and NoMad neighborhood for AI/software firms
stories.summary: Software company Distyl AI has leased the entire ninth floor at 135 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood, expanding its total footprint from 15,038 square feet to 30,076 square feet. The company arrived in December 2025 and is now doubling down less than a year later at $55 per square foot. Both leases run through January 2028. Distyl AI's expansion reflects confidence in NYC's tech market after establishing its second location there (with headquarters in San Francisco).
stories.impact: Tech tenant stability and expansion in NoMad/Flatiron signals sustained demand from AI/software companies for Manhattan office space, despite broader office headwinds. This supports office building valuations in the neighborhood and suggests ancillary residential demand from young, high-income tech workers. For multifamily developers, the concentration of venture-backed AI and software talent in NoMad/Flatiron reinforces the case for rental housing acquisition or development in adjacent residential submarkets (East Village, Lower East Side, Greenwich Village) targeting urban professionals with high income stability and retention.

stories.title: CIP Real Estate Buys San Gabriel Valley Industrial Park for $61M
stories.excerpt: The owner of a 200,049-square-foot industrial and flex complex in Los Angeles County’s San Gabriel Valley has unloaded the asset for $60.7 million. The Irvine-based CIP Real Estate acquired the Walnut Tech Business Center, an 11-building property at Valley Boulevard and Lemon Avenue in Walnut, from an affiliate of AEW. The complex contains 109 industrial, flex-office and service-commercial suites ranging from 640 to 8,400 square feet and is 92 percent leased. Property records show City National Bank provided $42.9 million in acquisition financing, arranged by JLL. CIP also plans a $3.5 million capital improvement program this year. The business center sits about a mile from the 60 Freeway and serves the City of Industry area, where small bay industrial space remains highly supply constrained. “Very few quality small bay industrial parks come available for sale in Southern California each year, especially a best-in-class project in this strategically important submarket of L.A. County,” CIP CEO Eric Smyth said in a statement. CIP represented itself in the transaction, while JLL’s Patrick Nally, Evan Moran and Chad Solomon represented AEW. The Walnut acquisition extends a busy stretch for CIP. The firm said it has closed more than $200 million in industrial park transactions over the past 90 days across Dallas, South Florida and Atlanta, bringing its industrial portfolio to more than $2.5 billion. The company owns and manages more than 12 million square feet of real estate. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIP Real Estate acquires Walnut Tech Business Center, San Gabriel Valley, for $60.7M; 200K SF, 109 small bay suites, 92% leased
City National Bank provided $42.9M financing via JLL; CIP budgets $3.5M capex; small bay industrial supply-constrained
Property located 1 mile from I-60, serves City of Industry—high-demand submarket for last-mile logistics and light manufacturing
stories.summary: CIP Real Estate acquired the Walnut Tech Business Center, a 200,049-square-foot industrial and flex complex in San Gabriel Valley's City of Industry area, for $60.7 million. The property contains 109 suites ranging from 640 to 8,400 square feet and is 92% leased. City National Bank provided $42.9 million in acquisition financing arranged by JLL. CIP plans a $3.5 million capital improvement program. The location is situated near the I-60 Freeway and serves one of Southern California's most supply-constrained small bay industrial submarkets.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance, but the acquisition underscores tight small bay industrial supply in LA County's Inland industrial corridor, driving investor demand and asset prices. Tight industrial supply supports logistics job growth and inbound investment to the City of Industry area, which could drive secondary population and housing demand in surrounding residential submarkets (Walnut, Diamond Bar, West Covina). Multifamily developers should monitor industrial absorption and new facility announcements in the City of Industry to identify emerging bedroom-community rental demand.

stories.title: Happier Grocery to Open Second NYC Location on the Upper East Side
stories.excerpt: A healthy grocery retailer is opening its second New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Happier Grocery has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at CSC Real Estate’s 210 East 86th Street, where it plans to open a health food store like its original one on Canal Street in the second half of 2027, according to landlord broker Avison Young. Avison Young did not immediately disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent along the nearby retail corridor of Third Avenue from East 60th to East 72nd streets was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “This lease transforms a long-vacant former movie theater space into a vibrant, wellness-focused destination that will add new energy to one of the Upper East Side’s most active retail corridors,” Avison Young’s Christian Stanton said in a statement. “Happier Grocery brings a fresh concept to the neighborhood, combining a curated, high-end grocery experience with a social atmosphere that complements the area’s strong residential base and established food retailers.” Stanton negotiated the deal on behalf of the landlord alongside Libby Hodes of Avison Young, as well as Max Swerdloff from Brand Urban. Newmark’s Brian Segall and Michael Cohen represented Happier Grocery in the deal. Happier Grocery opened its flagship location at 365 Canal Street in 2023, and has made a name for itself as a convenient stop for organic goodies. It also has a deli for hot food and a coffee bar at its Canal Street location. The grocer’s lease is the first deal to be signed at 210 East 86th Street after CSC Real Estate acquired it along with 206 East 86th Street and 205 East 85th Street for a total of $70 million in June, as Commercial Observer first reported. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Happier Grocery signs 20.5K SF lease at 210 East 86th St., Upper East Side; opening Q2 2027 in converted theater
Second NYC location for health grocery chain; Upper East Side Third Ave. corridor averaging $252/SF retail rent (Q2 2026)
Lease transforms long-vacant cultural space into wellness-focused retail destination in active retail corridor
stories.summary: Happier Grocery, a health-focused grocery retailer, has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at 210 East 86th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side, opening in the second half of 2027. The space is a converted former movie theater. The Upper East Side Third Avenue retail corridor was averaging $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026. The lease demonstrates continued retail vitality and conversion of cultural/entertainment spaces into retail in the neighborhood.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. The leasing signal that Upper East Side retail rents remain robust ($252/SF) and that quality retail concepts are willing to invest in the neighborhood supports property valuations and foot traffic in the area—factors that drive rental desirability for nearby residential buildings. However, the lease is a single retail transaction; it does not indicate significant supply constraints or demand shocks that would alter multifamily underwriting or development timing in Manhattan.

stories.title: Richard Born Part of Investor Group in BlackRock’s $245M Sale of 600 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Hotel investor Richard Born is the unnamed investor in 600 Third Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. Born joined L&L Infinite, a joint venture formed by former Silverstein Properties CEO Marty Burger and L&L Holding CEO David Levinson, as an investor in the $245 million purchase of the 42-story Midtown East office building from BlackRock, sources familiar with the deal told CO. Born now owns around 25 percent of the property, with each investor owning a roughly equal portion, a source said. Affiliates of Richard Mack’s Mack Real Estate Group, BLDG and BD Blakely were also part of the purchase. BD Blakely is an affiliate of BD Hotels, which was founded in 1986 by Born and Ira Drukier. Bloomberg first reported the sale, but did not mention Born’s involvement, reporting only that an institutional investor had teamed with L&L Infinite. The deal marks a big transformation for the office building, which BlackRock previously had a 99.5 percent stake in for roughly the past 20 years, with L&L Holding owning just 0.5 percent. Blackrock exited the deal to recycle capital, one source said. L&L Infinite and Born secured a $185 million acquisition loan from Bain Capital at closing to purchase the 1970-built property between East 39th and East 40th streets that was renovated in 2015. Newmark‘s Jordan Roeschlaub arranged the loan alongside Bain. Newmark also arranged the sale transaction with a team consisting of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger, Josh King, Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Doug Harmon. The property was 93 percent leased at the time of the deal, according to sources. Its anchor tenants include L-3 Communications, which occupies close to 59,000 square feet, along with law firms Polsinelli PC and Aaronson Rappaport Feinstein & Deutsch. Aaronson Rappaport renewed a 42,764-square-foot lease for its headquarters on the entire fifth and sixth floors in February 2025, CO first reported at the time. bullets: Richard Born (hotel investor, BD Hotels founder) joins L&L Infinite to acquire 600 Third Avenue from BlackRock for $245M
Born owns ~25% of 42-story Midtown East office tower; syndicate includes Mack Real Estate, BLDG, BD Blakely

stories.summary: Hotel investor Richard Born has joined a consortium led by L&L Infinite (Marty Burger and David Levinson) to acquire the 42-story office tower at 600 Third Avenue in Midtown East from BlackRock for $245 million. Born owns approximately 25 percent of the property, with other investors including Mack Real Estate Group, BLDG, and BD Blakely owning roughly equal stakes. The deal signals continued investor interest in trophy Midtown Manhattan office assets.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. The office acquisition by a hospitality-focused investor consortium suggests potential mixed-use conversion or repositioning play (hotel, residential, or cultural uses), but no details are provided. The deal reflects selective capital appetite for iconic Manhattan office in the hands of experienced operators; however, it does not indicate new multifamily demand drivers or supply constraints. Multifamily developers should monitor any announced conversion plans, as hotel-to-residential conversions in Midtown East could yield significant rental housing supply.

stories.title: JP Morgan Chase Sells South Florida Rental for $106M
stories.excerpt: J.P. Morgan Chase sold a garden-style multifamily property in Wellington, Fla., for $105.5 million after owning it for nearly a quarter century, according to property records. TA Realty purchased the 366-unit Polo Lakes community at 1950 Polo Lake Boulevard, just north of the Mall at Wellington Green, adjacent to Route 441, in the town best known as a leading equestrian hub. Built in 2000, the 19-acre property features 27 three-story buildings, as well as a basketball court and a pool. The sale equates to about $288,000 per apartment. J.P. Morgan Chase had purchased the 530,918-square-foot property for $47.4 million in 2002. TA Realty, which specializes in multifamily and industrial assets, has been making inroads in South Florida. Last year, the Boston-based firm paid $118 million for a 300-unit property in Pembroke Pines and $193 million for a 476-unit asset in Palm Beach Gardens. On the industrial front this year, TA Realty bought an industrial park near Miami International Airport for $48 million. A spokesperson for J.P. Morgan Chase’s asset management division declined to comment, while a representative for TA Realty did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: J.P. Morgan Chase sells Polo Lakes, Wellington, FL (366-unit garden-style) to TA Realty for $105.5M ($288K/unit)
JPM held asset 23 years (purchased 2002 for $47.4M); TA Realty expanding South Florida multifamily footprint aggressively
Wellington location near Route 441, adjacent to retail/entertainment; TA Realty deployed ~$311M South Florida multifamily in 18 months
stories.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase sold Polo Lakes, a 366-unit garden-style multifamily property in Wellington, Florida, to Boston-based TA Realty for $105.5 million ($288,000 per unit). The property, built in 2000 on 19 acres with 27 three-story buildings, was acquired by JPM in 2002 for $47.4 million. TA Realty has been aggressively acquiring multifamily assets in South Florida, including a $118 million deal on a 300-unit property in Pembroke Pines and a $193 million acquisition of a 476-unit asset in Palm Beach Gardens in the prior year.
stories.impact: TA Realty's aggressive South Florida multifamily acquisition strategy—deploying over $300M across three major deals in 18 months—signals strong investor confidence in market fundamentals (job growth, demographic migration, limited supply). The $288K/unit price on a stabilized, 24-year-old garden-style asset in Wellington suggests cap rates remain compressed and demand robust. For multifamily developers, the influx of institutional capital and stabilized-asset demand indicate a maturing South Florida market; developers should prioritize new development or value-add opportunities in secondary submarkets (Pembroke Pines, Palm Beach Gardens, Wellington exurbs) and emerging employment nodes to capture growth before institutional players and rents fully adjust.
